topic.title: Before the ECB decides: what its deposit rate moves for a euro saver and a variable mortgage

title: The ECB decides this month: what moves for savers and borrowers
description: The ECB's deposit rate is 2.5% after two rises this year. When it moves, here is what follows for a euro savings account and a variable mortgage, worked out by code. Speak to a licensed financial adviser in your country before making financial decisions. Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: Find your loan's next reset date

lines.text: €1,285 a month, not €1,252. One small rate rise on a variable mortgage.
In September, the European Central Bank raised its deposit rate to 2.5%. It decides again this month.
Up from 2.25%. It is what banks earn on cash parked at the ECB.
When it moves, savings follow slowly and partly. Variable loans follow at their next reset. Fixed loans don't move.
On €10,000 saved, 2% pays €200 a year. 2.25% pays €225.
So my loan can move faster than my savings?
Often. So know if your loan is variable, and when it resets.
Then the news won't catch you out.
